story_type: swimmer swept onto a sea rock by a wave, rescue watercraft pickup in surf, helicopter hoist from open water
hook: One wave swept him off the shore. This rock was all he could reach.
narration: One wave swept him off the shore. This rock was the only thing he could reach.
He swam there from a tide pool, then hurt his leg and could not get back.
Rescuers on a watercraft reached him and ran him out past the breaking surf.
A Coast Guard Jayhawk from Astoria was overhead, working with the Tillamook Fire Department.
A helicopter cannot hover tight against a cliff, so open water away from the rocks is the safer place to lift someone.
[short pause] Then the hoist lifted him up out of the sea.
outcome: The Jayhawk crew hoisted him at about one thirty and flew him to the park parking lot, where medics were waiting.
title: Swept off an Oregon shore by one wave
description:
On Dec. 26, 2015, a Coast Guard Air Station Astoria Jayhawk crew, working with the Tillamook Fire Department, rescued an 18-year-old swimmer who was swept onto a rock formation near Cape Lookout State Park, Oregon.

Footage: U.S. Coast Guard video courtesy of Coast Guard Air Station Astoria, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/444453/coast-guard-rescues-swimmer-distress-near-tillamook-ore

extra_sources.excerpt: A Coast Guard aircrew rescued a swimmer who was in distress and was reportedly injured near Cape Lookout State Park Saturday afternoon.

An MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter crew from Coast Guard Air Station Astoria hoisted the 18-year-old man around 1:30 p.m. and transported him to the Cape Lookout State Park parking lot where he was met by emergency medical response personnel.

The man was reportedly swimming in a tide pool with two friends when a wave swept him away from shore. The man was able to swim to a rock formation but could not safely get back to shore due to a reported leg injury.
